question: The Banking Codes and Standards Board of India (BCSBI) was set up on 18th February ____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**2006**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Banking Codes and Standards Board of India (BCSBI)** was established on **18th February 2006**, with the aim of improving the quality of banking services in India. It is an independent and autonomous body. 
• The BCSBI was constituted as per the recommendations of the **Committee on Procedures and Performance Audit on Public Services (CPPAPS)**, which was chaired by **S.S. Tarapore**, former Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). 
• The primary purpose of BCSBI is to ensure that banks adopt and implement voluntary codes, which set minimum standards for banking practices in India. 
• It works as an independent watchdog to monitor the compliance of member banks with the codes and standards they have committed to follow. 
• The BCSBI is funded by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and member banks, and it collaborates closely with the Indian Banks’ Association (IBA). 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Objectives of BCSBI:** 
• To ensure that **banks provide fair treatment** to their customers and do not discriminate against them. 
• To enhance the **transparency** in the services provided by banks, ensuring that terms and conditions are clearly communicated to customers. 
• To promote a culture of **responsible banking** by protecting the rights of customers and resolving grievances efficiently. 
• **Key Codes Released by BCSBI:** 
• The **Code of Bank’s Commitment to Customers:** First introduced in **2006**, this code lays down minimum service standards that banks should adhere to while dealing with individual customers. 
• The **Code of Bank’s Commitment to Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs):** Launched in **2008**, this code focuses on supporting the growth of MSEs by ensuring a fair and transparent banking process. 
• **Membership:** 
• Membership in BCSBI is voluntary, but most **scheduled commercial banks**, regional rural banks, and urban cooperative banks in India have joined the initiative. 
• **Role of RBI:** 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** plays a key role in supporting BCSBI by funding it initially and encouraging banks to become members and adopt the prescribed codes and standards. 
• **Importance of BCSBI:** 
• BCSBI ensures that banks provide better customer service and adhere to ethical banking practices. 
• It helps in creating awareness among customers about their rights and responsibilities, thereby promoting informed decision-making. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Background:** The need for BCSBI arose after concerns were raised about the lack of transparency and customer-centric practices in the Indian banking sector. The **Tarapore Committee** report highlighted these issues, leading to the formation of BCSBI. 
• **Customer Awareness:** BCSBI plays a vital role in educating customers about their rights under the codes and the steps they can take to resolve grievances. 
• **Monitoring and Compliance:** BCSBI monitors the performance of member banks through surveys and audits, ensuring they adhere to the commitments made under the codes. 
• **Grievance Redressal:** While BCSBI does not directly handle customer complaints, it ensures that member banks have robust grievance redressal mechanisms in place. 
• **Global Standards:** BCSBI’s efforts align with international best practices in banking, aiming to improve customer satisfaction and trust in the Indian banking system.
